sampling_dimensions.sampling_space_description: A sampling space for residents of the United States, based on the supplied demographic, occupation, opinion, interest, and habit data. The provided age, gender, race and ethnicity, household income, geography, marital status, religion, and selected public-opinion figures are represented as proportions where available. Some supplied figures are inconsistent or describe overlapping categories, especially political affiliation and religion; where a mutually exclusive distribution is needed, the output notes or accommodates that limitation. Fine-grained cultural profiles and the requested personality, attitude, taste, and belief weights are illustrative sampling variations rather than additional measured statistics.

dimensions.name: education_and_learning_profile
values: Is an infant or very young child who has not yet begun formal reading or writing, and communicates according to their developmental stage and available caregiver support.
Has had little or interrupted access to formal schooling and may have very limited literacy or numeracy, while retaining practical knowledge and skills learned through daily life.
Has difficulty reading complex material and may need plain-language explanations, translation, accessible formats, or patient one-to-one support.
Can read and write basic everyday language but has limited experience with formal academic study or specialized training.
Completed high school or an equivalent credential and relies on practical experience, workplace learning, and everyday information skills.
Attended community college, a certificate program, or technical training and has developed focused occupational skills without completing a four-year degree.
Earned a bachelor's degree and can apply academic, professional, or research skills in their work and personal interests.
Completed graduate or professional education and works with advanced knowledge in fields such as law, medicine, education, business, or public service.
Is a highly accomplished researcher, physician, engineer, scholar, or other specialist who contributes advanced expertise and may teach or mentor others.
Has exceptionally broad intellectual curiosity and advanced expertise, while remaining aware that specialized knowledge does not make someone equally informed about every topic.

dimensions.name: financial_situation
values: Experiences severe financial hardship, has little or no emergency savings, and may struggle to afford rent, utilities, food, healthcare, or reliable transportation.
Lives close to the edge of the household budget, pays essential bills but has little capacity to absorb an unexpected expense, missed paycheck, or medical bill.
Has a modest but relatively predictable income, uses budgeting to cover necessities, and is slowly building savings while managing debt or family obligations.
Feels financially stretched by inflation, housing, childcare, education, or healthcare costs despite having steady employment and a middle household income.
Has a stable income and some emergency savings, can usually meet regular expenses, and makes deliberate trade-offs between saving and discretionary purchases.
Is financially comfortable, has manageable debt and retirement contributions, and can afford occasional travel, hobbies, or household improvements.
Has substantial assets or a high income, uses professional financial advice, and has considerable flexibility in housing, education, healthcare, and leisure choices.
Has exceptional wealth and access to extensive financial resources, yet may still have complex obligations, business risks, family responsibilities, or concerns about preserving assets.
Is retired or living on a fixed income and carefully balances savings, pensions, Social Security, healthcare costs, housing, and support for family members.
Is temporarily experiencing a sharp financial reversal from job loss, illness, divorce, caregiving, disaster, or business failure, and is trying to recover stability.

dimensions.name: general_attitude
values: Approaches daily life with strong optimism, expects setbacks to be manageable, and actively encourages other people through generous and hopeful conversation.
Is generally positive and appreciative, notices small sources of enjoyment, and remains realistic about difficulties without allowing them to dominate every decision.
Is calm and pragmatically hopeful, prefers to assess evidence before reacting, and believes steady effort can improve many situations even when outcomes are uncertain.
Is open-minded and curious, listens to unfamiliar viewpoints, and can revise an opinion when new evidence or personal experience gives a persuasive reason.
Is sociable and welcoming but cautious about trust, offering kindness readily while taking time to assess whether another person is dependable.
Is emotionally mixed and somewhat changeable, showing enthusiasm when things are going well but becoming discouraged or irritable under sustained pressure.
Is guarded and skeptical, expects promises to be imperfectly kept, and prefers concrete evidence over reassuring language or grand claims.
Is persistently pessimistic, focuses on likely failure and disappointment, and may discount positive developments as temporary or undeserved.
Is apathetic or disengaged, finds it difficult to feel invested in work or community life, and often responds to choices with indifference or withdrawal.
Is unusually hostile and closed-minded, reacts to disagreement with contempt or aggression, and may deliberately undermine or mistreat others; this is an extreme fringe profile.

dimensions.name: culinary_tastes
values: Prefers familiar, traditional home cooking, such as regional family recipes, straightforward sides, and meals tied to personal or community traditions.
Enjoys bold heat and strongly seasoned food, seeking hot peppers, spice blends, and cuisines where intense flavor is central to the meal.
Prefers mild, simple flavors and may avoid hot spices, strong aromas, unfamiliar textures, or complicated combinations because they feel unpleasant or overwhelming.
Follows a vegetarian diet for ethical, religious, environmental, health, or personal reasons and seeks satisfying meals centered on vegetables, grains, beans, or dairy.
Follows a fully plant-based diet, checking ingredients carefully and choosing meals that avoid meat, fish, dairy, eggs, and other animal products.
Enjoys meat-centered meals, values familiar preparations such as grilling or roasting, and may see meat as an important source of flavor, tradition, or nourishment.
Is adventurous about food, regularly tries unfamiliar cuisines, ingredients, and cooking techniques, and enjoys discussing how dishes reflect their cultural origins.
Prefers convenient prepared meals, snacks, or takeout because of limited time, energy, cooking facilities, confidence, or interest in preparing food.
Enjoys baking and making desserts, from simple cookies and breads to elaborate pastries, and often shares homemade food with friends or family.
Has a restrictive or highly selective diet due to allergies, illness, sensory sensitivities, religious rules, or strong dislikes and may find eating out difficult.

dimensions.name: shopping_habits
values: Shops infrequently and deliberately, replacing items only when necessary and comparing prices carefully before committing to a purchase.
Plans purchases around a strict household budget, uses coupons or discount stores, and prioritizes durable essentials over optional upgrades.
Usually shops in physical stores to inspect products, ask questions, handle items, and combine errands with other activities.
Prefers online shopping for convenience, broad selection, accessibility, or time savings, and commonly checks reviews and delivery costs before buying.
Uses a balanced mix of in-store and online shopping, choosing the channel based on price, urgency, product type, and ease of access.
Shops frequently for household necessities and groceries, often planning lists and routines to manage a busy household or caregiving responsibilities.
Enjoys occasional spontaneous purchases and promotional offers but usually stays within a manageable personal spending limit.
Is brand-conscious and willing to pay more for familiar quality, customer service, design, or status, while still comparing some alternatives.
Is highly extravagant, making frequent luxury or impulse purchases with limited attention to long-term affordability; this is an uncommon extreme profile.
Avoids shopping whenever possible, feels overwhelmed by crowded stores or online choices, and may depend on another person or delivery service for essential purchases.

dimensions.name: health_consciousness
values: Is highly health-focused, schedules preventive care, exercises consistently, reads nutrition information, and makes daily choices with long-term wellbeing in mind.
Prioritizes physical and mental wellbeing when practical, while allowing flexibility for busy periods, family meals, celebrations, and personal enjoyment.
Uses a moderate routine of walking or other activity and tries to balance nutritious foods with convenient or indulgent choices without strict rules.
Pays attention to health mainly when symptoms arise, an appointment is due, or a family member's needs prompt a change in routine.
Has limited opportunity for exercise or preventive care because of cost, disability, demanding work, caregiving, transportation, or limited access to services.
Prefers conventional food and mainstream health advice, relies on familiar products, and is cautious about unverified supplements or wellness trends.
Seeks organic, minimally processed, or locally sourced foods when affordable and accessible, while recognizing that practical constraints sometimes determine purchases.
Enjoys indulgent foods and a sedentary leisure routine, rarely prioritizes exercise, and may find health recommendations inconvenient or difficult to sustain.
Lives with chronic illness, disability, pain, or mental health challenges that require substantial daily management, accommodations, medication, or support.
Engages in potentially harmful extremes, such as severely restricting food, overexercising, or ignoring urgent health needs; this represents a rare and concerning edge case.

dimensions.name: attitude_toward_new_products
values: Eagerly tests new products early, enjoys emerging technology and novel services, and tolerates occasional defects or inconvenience for the experience.
Is curious about new offerings but usually waits for credible reviews, clear pricing, and evidence that the product solves a genuine need.
Tries unfamiliar products when recommended by a trusted friend, relative, professional, or community member who understands their needs.
Adopts new products gradually, keeping familiar options available until the newer alternative has demonstrated reliability over time.
Is cautious about product claims, checks safety, privacy, durability, and return policies, and avoids purchasing based only on marketing or hype.
Prefers established brands and familiar products because consistency and predictability matter more than novelty or small possible improvements.
Is strongly resistant to changes in routines and products, viewing many new offerings as unnecessary, confusing, or designed to create avoidable costs.
Is enthusiastic about environmentally preferable, repairable, accessible, or ethically produced products even when adoption requires learning a new routine.
Avoids digital products and services when possible because of privacy concerns, accessibility barriers, limited connectivity, or low confidence using technology.
Is an extreme novelty seeker who buys untested products impulsively and disregards reasonable warnings, costs, or safety information.

dimensions.name: cultural_influences
values: Is strongly shaped by local community traditions, neighborhood relationships, regional foodways, and customs passed among nearby generations.
Combines local traditions with contemporary American popular culture, adopting some new habits while retaining familiar family and community practices.
Has a mostly homogeneous cultural environment and feels comfortable with familiar customs, language, food, and social expectations.
Moves among several cultural communities and adapts language, food, music, and social behavior to different family, work, or neighborhood settings.
Has deep ties to a heritage culture through family language, religious practice, food, music, or intergenerational relationships while also participating in broader U.S. life.
Is heavily influenced by global media, international travel, online communities, and popular culture from multiple countries rather than by a single local tradition.
Keeps traditional practices central to family life and is cautious about rapid cultural change, while still navigating contemporary workplaces and institutions.
Prefers contemporary and cosmopolitan cultural expression, regularly engaging with new music, art, ideas, and communities from around the world.
Has experienced migration, adoption, displacement, or mixed-heritage family history and actively negotiates a layered sense of belonging across places and traditions.
Feels culturally isolated or alienated, has limited access to community traditions or shared identity, and may be uncertain where they belong.

dimensions.name: travel_habits
values: Travels frequently for work or leisure, is comfortable with airports and changing schedules, and often plans trips across the country or internationally.
Takes occasional planned vacations, usually domestic, balancing travel interests with work schedules, household budgets, and caregiving responsibilities.
Enjoys short regional trips and day outings, preferring nearby parks, family visits, beaches, or small towns to long-distance travel.
Seeks adventurous travel, outdoor challenges, unfamiliar places, and flexible itineraries, while preparing carefully for safety and practical needs.
Prefers comfortable, predictable travel with reservations, familiar lodging, accessible transportation, and enough time to avoid rushed transitions.
Travels mainly to visit family, attend important events, or meet obligations, and does not necessarily consider travel a recreational interest.
Would like to travel more but is constrained by money, health, disability, work, documentation, caregiving, or limited transportation options.
Is a homebody who finds comfort and enjoyment in familiar surroundings and chooses local recreation over overnight or international trips.
Avoids travel because of anxiety, safety concerns, sensory overload, unfamiliar environments, or past negative experiences, even when opportunities are available.
Travels excessively or impulsively with little planning and may disregard health, financial, environmental, or safety consequences; this is an extreme profile.

dimensions.name: lifestyle
values: Maintains a highly active lifestyle with frequent walking, sports, outdoor recreation, and social commitments, adapting activity to health and access.
Balances work, family, exercise, hobbies, and downtime through a fairly structured routine, though competing responsibilities sometimes disrupt plans.
Lives a mostly sedentary routine because of desk work, limited energy, disability, transportation needs, or preference for screen-based leisure.
Has an urban lifestyle with nearby services, varied communities, public amenities, and many possible activities, while managing density, noise, and cost.
Has a rural lifestyle with greater distance between services, strong importance of local networks, and daily routines shaped by land, weather, or transportation.
Prefers minimalist living, owns relatively few possessions, and values simplicity, low maintenance, financial restraint, or environmental impact.
Enjoys a comfortable and moderately consumption-oriented lifestyle, making room for hobbies, dining out, home improvements, and occasional travel.
Favors an extravagant lifestyle, frequently spending on luxury goods, premium experiences, or expansive homes, sometimes with little concern for restraint.
Lives a family-centered or caregiving-focused routine, organizing much of the day around children, older relatives, household tasks, or supportive relationships.
Has a highly irregular lifestyle shaped by shift work, unstable housing, illness, crisis, or unpredictable obligations, making routines and leisure difficult to maintain.

dimensions.name: health_and_wellness_habits
values: Maintains regular physical activity through walking, exercise, sports, or other movement and tries to fit it into an otherwise busy schedule.
Has low physical-activity engagement, perhaps because of time, health, mobility, safety, cost, access, motivation, or work constraints.
Snacks frequently and often reaches for convenient foods such as cookies, reflecting preference, habit, stress, convenience, or availability.
Follows a consistent health routine involving preventive appointments, sleep practices, exercise, and food choices that support personal wellbeing.
Has inconsistent routines, alternating periods of healthy intentions with long stretches when fatigue, stress, or responsibilities take priority.
Uses exercise, meditation, prayer, hobbies, or social support to manage stress and preserve emotional wellbeing.
Copes with stress through comfort eating, smoking, inactivity, or other habits that may offer short-term relief but create longer-term concerns.
Lives with a condition or disability that makes standard health recommendations difficult to follow and may require adapted care and realistic goals.
Has limited access to primary care, nutritious food, safe exercise spaces, or reliable health information because of financial or geographic barriers.
Is intensely focused on health in a rigid or distressing way, or conversely disregards serious symptoms and care needs; these are uncommon extremes.

dimensions.name: sleep_patterns
values: Usually gets sufficient, restorative sleep and follows a fairly steady bedtime and waking schedule.
Often gets less sleep than they need because of work, study, caregiving, household responsibilities, or early travel schedules.
Keeps a late-night routine, often staying awake for work, entertainment, social media, gaming, or personal quiet time.
Works overnight or rotating shifts, so sleep timing changes substantially and rest may be interrupted by daytime responsibilities.
Experiences insomnia, restless sleep, nightmares, or frequent waking and may feel tired even after spending enough time in bed.
Has a flexible sleep schedule and sleeps well when able, but does not keep consistent hours from day to day.
Uses screens close to bedtime and finds it difficult to disengage from notifications, streaming, or online activity.
Has sleep disrupted by pain, illness, disability, mental distress, caregiving, noise, crowded housing, or unsafe surroundings.

dimensions.name: technology_use
values: Uses smartphones, computers, online services, and social media frequently for work, communication, news, entertainment, and everyday tasks.
Uses digital technology confidently but sets limits on notifications, screen time, online shopping, or social media to protect attention and privacy.
Relies heavily on social media for news, social connection, entertainment, and self-expression, checking platforms many times throughout the day.
Uses technology mainly for essential communication and practical tasks, avoiding unnecessary apps, subscriptions, or online accounts.
Is enthusiastic about gaming, streaming, smart devices, or emerging digital tools and enjoys learning new features.
Has limited digital access or skills because of cost, disability, connectivity, age, language, or lack of training, and may depend on others for online tasks.
Avoids social media or online services because of privacy concerns, misinformation, harassment, scams, or a preference for offline interaction.
Experiences excessive or compulsive screen use that interferes with sleep, work, relationships, safety, or other daily responsibilities.
